theory.title: A/An with professions and roles

theory_pt.title: A/An com profissões e cargos

theory.title: Questions with To Be and short answers

theory.title: Simple Present for Routine
theory.intro: In Week 2, the student learns to describe actions that happen regularly. The focus is not abstract grammar, but functional communication: saying what you do every day in study or work.

The basic pattern is: subject + base verb + complement.
Examples: I work with data. I study every morning. We use Slack.

theory.title: Verb + Object in Daily Tech English
theory.intro: This lesson trains a high-value structure for beginners: a simple verb followed by a direct object. This is one of the fastest ways to build professional communication.
content: Many routine sentences in English follow this pattern: subject + verb + object.

theory.title: Questions with Do

aulas.subtitulo: Clock In — Hours and Time Expressions

lessonMeta.focus: Basic clock time and daily time expressions
lessonMeta.canDo: I can say basic times and talk about simple moments of the day.
outputTargets: Say basic times correctly.
Use at + time and in the morning/afternoon/evening.
Connect time to a simple action.

arena.speech:
Mission: now you add time to your English.

In professional life, routine is not enough. You also need to say when things happen.

It is nine o'clock.
At eight o'clock, I study.
In the morning, I read messages.

This week, you learn to organize actions in time.

options.feedback: Excellent. That is a correct sentence connecting time and action.
Not correct here. Use at with clock time: At eight o'clock, I study.

options.text: At eight o'clock, I am study.
options.feedback: The time phrase is correct, but the verb structure is not. Say: At eight o'clock, I study.

theory.title: Basic Time in English
theory.intro: This lesson introduces the language of clock time and daily time reference. The learner begins to place routine actions on a simple timeline, which is essential for schedule talk in work and study environments.
content: Use at with specific clock times: at eight o'clock, at nine.
Use in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening for broad parts of the day.
Use at night instead of in the night in basic routine descriptions.
The structure It is + time is useful to identify the hour.
The structure At + time, I + verb is useful to describe scheduled routine actions.
examples: In the morning, I read messages.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: In eight o'clock. → Correct: At eight o'clock.
Incorrect: In the night, I study. → Better at this stage: At night, I study.
Incorrect: It is nine clock. → Correct: It is nine o'clock.

theory_pt.title: Horas e Tempo Básico em Inglês
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição introduz a linguagem de horas do relógio e referência de tempo diário. O aluno começa a colocar ações de rotina em uma linha do tempo simples, o que é essencial para falar de horários em ambientes de trabalho e estudo.
content: Use at com horas específicas do relógio: at eight o'clock, at nine.
Use in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening para partes amplas do dia.
Use at night em vez de in the night em descrições básicas de rotina.
A estrutura It is + hora é útil para identificar o horário.
A estrutura At + hora, I + verbo é útil para descrever ações de rotina programadas.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: In eight o'clock. → Correto: At eight o'clock.
Incorreto: In the night, I study. → Melhor nesta fase: At night, I study.
Incorreto: It is nine clock. → Correto: It is nine o'clock.

lessonMeta.focus: Daily schedule sequencing with simple present
lessonMeta.canDo: I can describe a basic daily schedule in order.

arena.speech:
Mission: build a timeline for your day.

Now you do more than say actions. You organize them:

At eight, I study.
Then, I check my tasks.
After that, I read messages.
At night, I write notes.

options.feedback: Perfect. This is a correct sequencing sentence for a schedule.

options.text: Then, I am check my tasks.

theory.title: Sequencing a Simple Schedule
theory.intro: The learner now moves from isolated time references to a short ordered schedule. This supports both spoken routine descriptions and basic professional time management language.
content: A schedule description often combines time markers and routine verbs.
Useful sequence markers at this level are: then and after that.
The structure stays simple: time marker + subject + verb + complement.
The student should prioritize logical order and sentence stability.
A short schedule is more effective than a long unstable paragraph.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: Then I am check my tasks. → Correct: Then, I check my tasks.
Incorrect: After that I reads messages. → Correct: After that, I read messages.
Incorrect: At night I am write notes. → Correct: At night, I write notes.

theory_pt.title: Sequenciando uma Agenda Simples
theory_pt.intro: O aluno agora passa de referências de tempo isoladas para uma agenda curta e ordenada. Isso apoia tanto as descrições faladas de rotina quanto a linguagem básica de gerenciamento de tempo profissional.
content: Uma descrição de agenda frequentemente combina marcadores de tempo e verbos de rotina.
Marcadores de sequência úteis neste nível são: then (depois/então) e after that (depois disso).
A estrutura permanece simples: marcador de tempo + sujeito + verbo + complemento.
O aluno deve priorizar a ordem lógica e a estabilidade da frase.
Uma agenda curta é mais eficaz do que um parágrafo longo e instável.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: Then I am check my tasks. → Correto: Then, I check my tasks.
Incorreto: After that I reads messages. → Correto: After that, I read messages.

aulas.subtitulo: Are You Free? — Availability and Meetings

lessonMeta.focus: Basic availability questions and meeting language
lessonMeta.canDo: I can ask and answer simple questions about availability and meeting times.
outputTargets: Ask about simple availability.

arena.speech:
Mission: talk about availability.

In work and study life, you need to say if you are free or busy.

Are you free at nine?
Yes, I am.
No, I'm not.
The meeting is at ten.

This is essential for coordination.

options.feedback: Excellent. That is a correct and useful availability question.
Not correct. With free, use the verb to be: Are you free at nine?
Use at with clock time: Are you free at nine?

theory.title: Availability and Simple Meeting Coordination
theory.intro: This lesson introduces basic availability language for study and work coordination. The learner uses already known structures with new communicative purpose: scheduling and responding to time requests.
content: Use Are you free...? to ask about availability.
Use Yes, I am. and No, I'm not. to answer clearly.
Use The meeting is at + time to communicate a simple schedule fact.
This lesson combines Week 1 be-questions with Week 3 time language.
The target is functional coordination, not complex calendar language.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: Do you free at nine? → Correct: Are you free at nine?
Incorrect: The meeting is in ten. → Correct: The meeting is at ten.
Incorrect: Yes, I do. → For this be-question, use: Yes, I am.

theory_pt.title: Disponibilidade e Coordenação Simples de Reuniões
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição introduz a linguagem básica de disponibilidade para coordenação de estudo e trabalho. O aluno usa estruturas já conhecidas com um novo propósito comunicativo: agendar e responder a solicitações de tempo.
content: Use Are you free...? para perguntar sobre disponibilidade.
Use Yes, I am. e No, I'm not. para responder de forma clara.
Use The meeting is at + horário para comunicar um fato simples da agenda.
Esta lição combina as perguntas com 'be' da Semana 1 com a linguagem de tempo da Semana 3.
O alvo é a coordenação funcional, não uma linguagem de calendário complexa.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: Do you free at nine? → Correto: Are you free at nine?
Incorreto: The meeting is in ten. → Correto: The meeting is at ten.
Incorreto: Yes, I do. → Para esta pergunta com 'be', use: Yes, I am.

theory.title: Building a Simple Timetable
theory.intro: The final lesson of Week 3 integrates time language, routine descriptions and availability into a practical daily timetable. This creates a stronger sense of functional control in professional English.
content: A timetable is a short organized description of what happens and when it happens.
At A1 level, the student should use short complete sentences with predictable structure.
Useful patterns are: At + time, I + verb and I am free at + time.
The learner can combine specific times and broad parts of the day.

theory_pt.title: Construindo um Quadro de Horários Simples
theory_pt.intro: A última lição da Semana 3 integra linguagem de tempo, descrições de rotina e disponibilidade em um quadro de horários diário prático. Isso cria um senso mais forte de controle funcional no inglês profissional.
content: Um quadro de horários é uma descrição curta e organizada do que acontece e quando acontece.
No nível A1, o aluno deve usar frases curtas e completas com estrutura previsível.
Padrões úteis são: At + hora, I + verbo e I am free at + hora.
O aluno pode combinar horários específicos e partes amplas do dia.
Uma produção final bem-sucedida soa simples, clara e organizada.
examples: Às dez, eu tenho uma reunião.
À tarde, eu trabalho no meu projeto.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: In ten, I have a meeting. → Correto: At ten, I have a meeting.
Incorreto: I free at five. → Correto: I am free at five.
Incorreto: In the afternoon, I am work on my project. → Correto: In the afternoon, I work on my project.

theory.title: Days of the Week in English
theory.intro: This lesson introduces the basic weekly cycle in English. The learner connects routine language to days of the week, which is essential for planning classes, meetings and simple professional events.
content: Use on with days of the week: on Monday, on Friday.
Days of the week are usually capitalized in English: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.
The pattern On + day, I + verb is highly useful for A1 planning language.
You can also use My meeting is on Wednesday to place an event in the week.
At this stage, the priority is correct day reference and sentence stability.
examples: On Friday, I review my project.

Incorrect: My meeting is in Wednesday. → Correct: My meeting is on Wednesday.

theory.title: Simple Dates in English
theory.intro: This lesson introduces calendar dates in a controlled and functional way. The goal is not full calendar mastery, but the ability to recognize and use basic month + day structures in professional or academic contexts.
content: A simple English date can be expressed with month + ordinal day: March tenth, April fifth.
Use on with dates when connecting them to events: The meeting is on April fifth.
At this stage, the learner does not need full calendar complexity; simple event-date connections are enough.
Date language is especially useful for classes, meetings, interviews and deadlines.
The structure should remain stable and controlled.
examples: The class is on March twelfth.
The meeting is on April fifth.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: The class is in March twelfth. → Correct: The class is on March twelfth.
Incorrect: It is March ten. → Acceptable in some contexts, but this course models: It is March tenth.
Incorrect: The meeting is on April five. → Better in this model: The meeting is on April fifth.
